metadata.owner: Marlandoj (operator); Alaric (Chief of Staff) - spec author
metadata.releaseTier: v1.0 public alpha -> free public beta -> GA (free, anonymous, operator-funded)

factory.area: Net-new private monorepo implementation of the free anonymous Fountain-to-MP4 vertical slice. Public branding, public deployment, and live paid generation remain blocked by ADR-0020 until name, counsel, benchmark, and operator-budget gates pass.

mission.statement: Build Hollywood Video: a free, anonymous, script-first AI filmmaking studio in which any visitor pastes a Fountain screenplay and, without an account, an upload, or a payment, receives a watchable H.264 MP4 assembled from AI-generated shots. The operator funds all inference and rendering; the product earns goodwill, a public benchmark, and a distribution moat, not subscription revenue.
mission.firstExperience: A new visitor pastes a 5-page Fountain script, sees a parsed preview, approves the animatic at the single human-in-the-loop gate, and - with no signup, no card, and no watermark - downloads a watchable H.264 MP4 within the published time-to-MP4 target.
qualities: zero-friction anonymous access (no account, no card, no watermark)
operator-funded (no user billing of any kind)
evidence-governed (24-shot benchmark with regression gates in CI)
reproducible (deterministic hashes; byte-identical output for identical inputs)
fail-closed safety (any missing safety gate blocks generation)
self-hostable (single docker compose on one 4xA100 machine)
mission.releaseTier: v1.0 public alpha -> free public beta -> GA (free, anonymous, operator-funded)
mission.excludedTier: paid tiers, freemium, subscriptions, pass-through provider charges, required accounts or free accounts (rejected by ADR-0018)

constraints.text: All inference and rendering is operator-funded; no user billing, subscription, credit ledger, or payment of any kind exists in the product.
No account, no email, no cookie: anonymous project access is via a signed, expiring (72 h) token embedded in a URL.
Fail-closed safety: any missing safety gate blocks generation rather than warning.
Self-hostable: a single docker compose up runs the full stack with no cloud-specific dependencies.
Reproducible: the same script, model, seed, and parameters produce a byte-identical MP4; the 24-shot benchmark is a CI artifact with deterministic hashes.
Hard monthly cost cap below $5,000 with auto-throttle at 80% of budget, rejection at 100%, and a per-job cost cap (default $5/shot).
The animatic approval is the only human-in-the-loop gate in v1.

Security and privacy baseline: mTLS between internal services, signed URLs for artifact access, no secrets in images, no cookies, no tracking pixels; IP addresses logged for rate limiting only and deleted after 30 days.
Evidence-gated changes: the 24-shot benchmark runs in CI on every model/provider change and a regression greater than 5% on any metric blocks merge.

antiGoals.text: No user accounts, authentication, or payment - signup itself is an access barrier (ADR-0018).
No feature that requires a user to spend money; no freemium, subscriptions, or pass-through provider charges.
No real-time collaborative editing in v1.
No full non-linear editing timeline in v1; v1 is linear assembly only.
No 4K or HDR output in v1; v1 targets 1080p H.264.
No mobile-native app in v1; responsive web only.
No public API in v1; an internal API exists and a public API is a post-alpha consideration.
No audio mixing, music licensing, or localization in v1.

protectedCapabilities.text: Anonymous zero-charge access: the complete core journey completes without identity or payment.
Fail-closed content safety: every prompt passes the moderation layer before reaching any provider; blocked prompts return a polite refusal.
Provenance: every generated frame carries a C2PA-style content credential and a downloadable reproducibility manifest ships with the MP4.
Hard operator budget: auto-throttle at 80% of budget and rejection at 100% keep monthly spend under cap.
Deterministic reproducibility of pipeline output and benchmark runs.
Data minimization: no personal data collected and anonymous projects auto-delete after 30 days.

scopeCutOrder: Elevated capacity tier (FR-030) - operator-granted only; the free tier is the product
TTS voiceover (FR-041) - fall back to silent cuts with burned-in subtitles
Extended export formats (ProRes, DNxHR) and 4K (FR-11.3 deferred item; v1.1)
Proxy editing / drag-to-reorder timeline (FR-9.4 deferred item; v1.1)
Localization and multi-language dubbing (FR-10.3 deferred item; v2)
Real-time collaborative editing (never in v1 scope)

decisions.question: Is 'Hollywood Video' the final product name, or do we adopt a cleared alternative?
decisions.requiredEvidence: Trademark clearance in relevant classes, documented in ADR (FR-1.4, task HV-001 / ZOU-1480)
decisions.resolution: Proceed under the working name 'Hollywood Video'. HV-001 performs clearance in parallel (FR-004, risk R5) and documents the result in an ADR; if the name is blocked, adopt the pre-cleared fallback. No build work is blocked pending clearance.

decisions.question: Which video generation provider is the v1 default?
decisions.requiredEvidence: HV-001 24-shot benchmark results: visual quality, continuity, latency, and cost per shot (FR-002)
decisions.resolution: Per ADR-0020, implement the provider-neutral adapter and deterministic mock first. HV-001 selects the production primary and secondary only after the 24-shot benchmark and explicit operator budget approval; paid generation remains disabled until then.

decisions.question: Which TTS provider serves alpha voiceover (FR-10.1)?
decisions.requiredEvidence: Alpha trial: voiceover quality on dialogue lines plus cost at ~200 minutes of audio per month
decisions.resolution: Per ADR-0020, Piper is the self-hosted alpha default. Caption-only silent output is the required degradation path when TTS is unavailable; paid TTS remains optional and disabled pending later evidence and operator approval.

decisions.question: Which object storage backend serves FR-2.4?
options: Cloudflare R2 (free tier, no egress fees)
decisions.requiredEvidence: M1 deployment test against the portability NFR (no cloud-specific dependencies in compose)
decisions.resolution: The contract is the S3-compatible interface (FR-008). Self-hosted compose ships MinIO to satisfy the portability NFR (NFR-006); the operator-hosted deployment may use Cloudflare R2. The final hosted backend is confirmed at M1; neither choice changes the interface or any requirement.

decisions.question: What legal entity or liability shield operates the free public service?
options: Operate under the existing Zouroboros umbrella
decisions.requiredEvidence: Counsel review of ToS, privacy policy, and content policy before public launch (FR-056)
decisions.resolution: Per ADR-0020, development and private staging proceed under the existing Zouroboros umbrella. Public deployment, public terms, and public branding remain fail-closed until counsel reviews the operating entity, liability boundary, ToS, privacy policy, and content policy under HV-014.

requirements.text: Define a 24-shot benchmark script as a fixed Fountain file versioned in git.
Benchmark measures per-shot generation latency, total pipeline time, visual quality (CLIP/FID or equivalent), continuity (face/scene consistency), and cost per shot.
Benchmark runs in CI on every model/provider change; a regression greater than 5% on any metric blocks merge.
Product name clearance: verify the chosen name is not trademarked in relevant classes and document the result in an ADR.
Monorepo with separate packages: frontend, api, parser, planner, generator, assembler, safety, queue, benchmarks.
CI pipeline: lint, typecheck, unit tests, integration tests, benchmark (GPU runner), build, deploy.
Anonymous access: project creation returns a signed, expiring (72 h) token embedded in a URL; no email, no cookie, no account.
All artifacts (shots, renders, MP4s) go to S3-compatible object storage with a 30-day auto-delete lifecycle for anonymous projects.
Job system: persistent, idempotent jobs (Redis + worker pool); every job has a retry policy, timeout, and cost tracker.
Telemetry: structured JSON logs, Prometheus metrics, Grafana dashboards; every generation job emits cost, latency, model, and quality metadata.
Parse standard Fountain format: scene headings, action, dialogue, transitions, parentheticals.
Editor: paste or upload .fountain with live preview of parsed structure (scenes, shots, characters).
Protected text: users can mark lines as locked (e.g., brand names, legal text) that the generator must not alter.
Revision history: each edit creates a version; regeneration can target any prior version.
Validation: reject scripts over 30 pages (v1 cap), warn above 20 scenes, flag unparseable constructs.
Auto-generate a creative bible per project: character descriptions, setting palette, tone keywords, style references.
Rights and consent: require user attestation (checkbox) that they hold rights to all referenced IP, characters, and locations.
Provenance: every generated frame carries a C2PA-style content credential (model, prompt hash, timestamp, seed).
Provenance manifest: downloadable JSON alongside the MP4 listing all models, prompts, seeds, and parameter hashes for full reproducibility.
LLM-driven shot planner converts the parsed script into a shot list (shot type, duration, camera angle, motion, dialogue overlay).
Storyboard: per-shot thumbnail image (text-to-image) showing composition, character placement, and setting.
Animatic: auto-assemble storyboard stills with timing and dialogue audio (TTS) into a rough-cut video for review before expensive video generation.
User review gate: the user must approve the animatic (or request edits) before video generation begins; this is the only human-in-the-loop gate in v1.
Provider adapter interface generate(prompt, seed, params) -> video_clip with implementations for Runway, Pika, Kling, local ComfyUI, and at least one open-weight model.
Durable generation jobs survive worker restarts, checkpoint at frame boundaries, and resume on retry.
Safe submission: all prompts pass the safety/moderation layer before reaching any provider; blocked prompts return a polite refusal, not an error.
Provider failover: if the primary provider times out or errors, retry on the configured secondary before failing the job.
Cost guardrails: per-job cost cap (configurable, default $5/shot); if exceeded, the job is cancelled and the user is notified.
Fair queue: each anonymous project gets a weighted fair share of GPU time; no project can starve another.
Capacity tiers: free (default) = 1 concurrent project, max 24 shots, 720p, standard queue; elevated (operator-granted) = 3 concurrent, 60 shots, 1080p, priority queue.
Operator cost dashboard: real-time spend per day/week/month, per project, per provider, per shot type.
Auto-throttle: at 80% of monthly budget, new free-tier projects queue behind existing jobs; at 100%, new projects are rejected with a capacity-full message.
Cost accounting: every job records {provider, model, prompt_tokens, output_frames, gpu_seconds, total_cost_usd}, aggregated to daily/weekly/monthly rollups.
Continuity packet: per character, a reference image set plus text description, injected into every shot prompt that features the character.
Shot-to-shot continuity check compares adjacent shots for character consistency (face embedding distance), lighting, and palette; shots below threshold are flagged.
Human review queue: flagged shots appear in an operator review panel where the operator approves, regenerates, or manually adjusts.
Repair loop: a shot failing continuity after regeneration (max 2 retries) is marked 'degraded' and the final MP4 carries a metadata note.
Auto-assembly: concatenate approved shots in script order, apply crossfades (0.5 s default), burn in dialogue subtitles (optional toggle).
Inline viewer: stream the assembled video in-browser (HLS) with per-shot timestamps, thumbnails, and regeneration buttons.
Export: H.264 MP4, 1080p, 30 fps, AAC audio; download link valid for 30 days.
Alpha: auto-generate voiceover from dialogue lines using TTS (ElevenLabs or an open-source alternative).
Alpha: SRT/VTT captions burned in or provided as a sidecar file.
Export pipeline is ffmpeg-based and deterministic: same inputs produce the same output hash.
Every exported MP4 passes ffprobe checks (codec, resolution, duration, bitrate) before the download link is issued.
Signed review links: any project can be shared via a URL with read-only or approve/deny permission; no account required.
Approval workflow: creator submits, reviewer views, reviewer approves or requests changes (free-text note), creator regenerates or finalizes.
Link hygiene: review links expire after 7 days or 3 views (configurable) and are revocable by the creator.
Public status page: current queue depth, estimated wait time, system health; no PII.
Operator console (authenticated, internal): job monitoring, queue management, project kill-switch, cost alerts, provider health.
Support: in-app 'Report an issue' form (no account; attaches project ID + anonymized logs), routed to the operator inbox.
Analytics: anonymized, aggregated usage metrics (projects created, shots generated, completion rate, avg time-to-MP4); no individual tracking.
Terms of Service: clear, plain language - free use, operator-funded, no SLA, content is the user's responsibility, operator can delete any project.
Privacy: no personal data collected; IP address logged for rate limiting only and deleted after 30 days; no cookies; no tracking pixels.
Content policy prohibits: (a) identifiable real persons without consent, (b) CSAM or sexual content involving minors, (c) deepfake political content, (d) trademark-infringing brand content.
Takedown: DMCA-style form; the operator can takedown any project within 24 h of a verified request; takedown is logged and irreversible.
Legal review: ToS, privacy policy, and content policy reviewed by counsel before public launch.
Data retention: anonymous project data auto-deletes after 30 days; the operator can manually extend for benchmark purposes (logged).
Load test: sustain 50 concurrent projects and 500 shots in queue with p99 shot latency under 120 s.
Security pen test on auth tokens, rate limiting, file upload, and API; fix all critical/high findings before launch.
Free public beta: soft launch to 100 invited users for 2 weeks; monitor cost, quality, and failure rates.
GA launch: public URL, status page live, social announcement, benchmark results published.
Post-launch cadence: weekly cost review, monthly benchmark re-run, quarterly capacity planning.
Performance: p99 shot generation under 90 s (720p, 5 s clip); end-to-end script-to-MP4 under 15 min for a 12-shot short.
Availability: 99% monthly uptime for the public site; GPU-maintenance downtime acceptable with under 4 h notice.
Scalability: horizontal GPU worker scaling; queue depth over 1,000 jobs without degradation.
Security: all internal service traffic over mTLS; signed URLs for artifact access; no secrets in images.
Observability: 100% of jobs produce structured logs; dashboards for queue depth, cost/hour, error rate, and p50/p95/p99 latency.
Portability: docker compose up on a single 4xA100 machine runs the full stack; no cloud-specific dependencies.
Reproducibility: given the same script, model, seed, and parameters, the output MP4 is byte-identical.
Accessibility: WCAG 2.1 AA; all interactive elements keyboard-navigable; captions on all exported video.

verifications.method: CI lint + typecheck across all monorepo packages
verifications.threshold: Zero errors; every commit must pass

verifications.method: Unit tests for parser, planner, queue, cost accounting, editor state, and creative-bible generation
verifications.threshold: 100% pass; line coverage >= 90% on parser, planner, and queue

verifications.method: Fountain parser conformance suite: scene headings, action, dialogue, transitions, parentheticals, protected text, 30-page cap, 20-scene warning, and unparseable-construct fixtures
verifications.threshold: All fixtures parse to the expected AST; cap/warn/flag behaviors match FR-015

verifications.method: Full-pipeline integration on the compose stack with a stubbed provider: script -> shot plan -> storyboard -> animatic -> generation -> assembly -> export
verifications.threshold: A 12-shot short completes end-to-end deterministically

verifications.method: Provider adapter contract tests per implementation (generate(prompt, seed, params) -> clip) including the failover path
verifications.threshold: All adapters return clips with expected metadata; primary timeout routes to the secondary, which completes the job

verifications.method: Safety gate battery of prohibited prompts: identifiable real persons, minors, political deepfakes, trademarked brands
verifications.threshold: 100% blocked before any provider call; polite refusal returned; zero provider submissions

verifications.method: Run the 24-shot benchmark (fixed versioned Fountain, pinned model + seed)
verifications.threshold: Baseline recorded; regression > 5% on any metric blocks merge; per-shot latency, cost, quality, and continuity recorded

verifications.method: Continuity evaluation: face-embedding distance between adjacent shots featuring the same character, plus lighting and palette comparison
verifications.threshold: Flagged shots surface in the operator review queue; >= 80% of shot pairs pass at the post-GA target

verifications.method: Anonymous journey test: fresh visitor pastes a script, receives a tokenized URL, completes rights attestation, approves the animatic, and downloads the MP4
verifications.threshold: Zero account/email/card prompts; token expires at 72 h; generation is blocked until animatic approval

verifications.method: Provenance check on export: C2PA-style per-frame credentials plus the downloadable manifest
verifications.threshold: Every frame carries model, prompt hash, timestamp, and seed; the manifest lists all models, prompts, seeds, and parameter hashes

verifications.method: Export validation: ffprobe (codec, resolution, duration, bitrate, audio) plus deterministic re-export hash comparison
verifications.threshold: 100% of exports pass ffprobe; identical inputs produce identical MP4 hashes

verifications.method: Durability test: kill the generation worker mid-job, then restart it
verifications.threshold: Job resumes from the last frame-boundary checkpoint with no duplicate or lost shots; idempotent

verifications.method: Load test: 50 concurrent projects, 500 shots in queue
verifications.threshold: p99 shot latency < 120 s; no degradation at queue depth > 1,000 jobs

verifications.method: Cost accounting audit: compare job cost records against provider invoices over a 2-week window
verifications.threshold: Daily/weekly/monthly rollups match provider invoices within 5%

verifications.method: Budget enforcement simulation: drive monthly spend to 80% and 100% of budget
verifications.threshold: At 80% new free-tier projects queue behind existing jobs; at 100% new projects are rejected with the capacity message; per-job cap (default $5/shot) cancels and notifies

verifications.method: Free public beta: 100 invited users for 2 weeks
verifications.threshold: Completion rate >= 70%; median time-to-MP4 < 12 min; monthly cost < $5,000; uptime >= 99%

verifications.method: Penetration test: auth tokens, rate limiting, file upload, API
verifications.threshold: No open critical or high findings at launch

verifications.method: Security static audit: secret scan of images and repo, mTLS configuration, signed-URL enforcement, cookie/tracking-pixel scan
verifications.threshold: Zero secrets in images; internal traffic mTLS; artifact access via signed URLs only; no cookies or tracking pixels

verifications.method: Counsel review of ToS, privacy policy, and content policy
verifications.threshold: Documented sign-off before public launch

verifications.method: WCAG 2.1 AA audit of the public UI (keyboard navigation, contrast) plus caption check on all exported video
verifications.threshold: Passes the automated and manual AA checklist; captions present on every export

verifications.method: Review link contract tests: permission levels, 7-day/3-view expiry, creator revocation
verifications.threshold: Read-only links cannot approve; expired or revoked links are rejected; revocation is immediate

verifications.method: Takedown flow test: verified request -> project removal
verifications.threshold: Takedown completes, is logged, and is irreversible; artifacts inaccessible afterward

verifications.method: Retention test: age anonymous projects past 30 days
verifications.threshold: Projects and artifacts auto-delete at 30 days; operator extensions logged; IPs deleted after 30 days

verifications.method: Trademark clearance search for the product name in relevant classes
verifications.threshold: Clearance documented in an ADR; fallback name pre-cleared if blocked

verifications.method: Fresh docker compose up deployment on a single 4xA100 host, followed by the end-to-end pipeline run
verifications.threshold: Full stack healthy; the 12-shot e2e completes; no cloud-specific dependencies

verifications.method: Five-user pilot: external users each produce a 60-second MP4
verifications.threshold: 5/5 complete with zero operator intervention

acceptanceCriteria.text: The 24-shot benchmark is defined (fixed, versioned Fountain file) and runs end-to-end with baseline metrics recorded: per-shot latency, total pipeline time, visual quality (CLIP/FID or equivalent), continuity, and cost per shot.
CI runs the benchmark on every model/provider change and blocks merge on a regression greater than 5% on any metric.
Name clearance for 'Hollywood Video' (or the pre-cleared fallback) is documented in an ADR.
Anonymous project creation returns a signed 72 h URL token, and the complete core journey finishes with no account, email, or card.
The 9-package monorepo exists and CI is green through lint, typecheck, unit, integration, and build stages.
The Fountain editor and parser pass the conformance suite, including protected text, 30-page rejection, 20-scene warning, and unparseable-construct flagging, with per-edit version history.
The creative bible auto-generates per project, rights attestation is captured, and every export carries C2PA-style credentials plus the downloadable provenance manifest.
A 12-shot short is produced end-to-end (script to MP4) with fewer than 2 continuity failures.
All provider submissions pass the safety gate; the prohibited-prompt battery is 100% blocked with a polite refusal and zero provider calls.
The per-job cost cap (default $5/shot) cancels over-cap jobs and notifies the user; every job records provider, model, prompt_tokens, output_frames, gpu_seconds, and total_cost_usd with rollups.
Capacity tiers are enforced (free: 1 concurrent / 24 shots / 720p; elevated: 3 / 60 / 1080p) and auto-throttle is verified at 80% (queue behind) and 100% (reject with capacity message).
The continuity check flags below-threshold shots to the operator review queue; the repair loop retries at most twice, then marks the shot 'degraded' with a metadata note in the final MP4.
Auto-assembly (script order, 0.5 s crossfades, optional subtitles), the HLS viewer, and export (H.264 1080p 30 fps AAC, 30-day link) work; every export passes ffprobe and re-export is byte-identical.
Alpha TTS voiceover from dialogue lines and SRT/VTT captions (burned in or sidecar) are present on exports.
Accountless review links support read-only and approve/deny permissions, expire after 7 days or 3 views, and are revocable by the creator.
The public status page, operator console, support form, and anonymized analytics are live; no PII on any public surface; IPs delete after 30 days; no cookies or tracking pixels.
ToS and the content policy (four prohibitions) are live and counsel-reviewed; takedown completes within 24 h of a verified request and is logged and irreversible.
Free public beta completes: 100 invited users over 2 weeks with completion rate >= 70%, median time-to-MP4 < 12 min, monthly cost < $5,000, and uptime >= 99%.

The load test passes (50 concurrent projects, 500 queued shots, p99 < 120 s), the pen test has no open critical or high findings, and the GA launch is live (public URL, status page, announcement, published benchmark results).
Post-launch cadence is operational: weekly cost review, monthly benchmark re-run, quarterly capacity planning.
The public site sustains >= 99% monthly uptime during the beta window.
The public UI meets WCAG 2.1 AA (all interactive elements keyboard-navigable) and every exported video carries captions.
The full stack runs via a single docker compose up on a 4xA100 machine with no cloud-specific dependencies.
Durable, idempotent jobs survive worker restart via frame-boundary checkpoints; every job carries a retry policy, timeout, and cost tracker.
Under mixed load, no anonymous project starves another (weighted fair share of GPU time).
Provider failover: a primary provider timeout or error retries on the configured secondary before the job fails.
Revision history: each edit creates a version and regeneration can target any prior version.
Anonymous projects and artifacts auto-delete after 30 days (S3 lifecycle); operator extensions are logged.
Five external users each produce a 60-second MP4 without operator intervention (M3 gate).

milestones.name: Assembly, export, and accountless review (HV-009 to HV-012)

humanCriteria.question: Do the animatic and continuity results from the CS-001 and CS-007 runs meet the narrative bar for a free public release?
Are the beta economics (cost per completed MP4, failure rate) sustainable under the < $5,000/month cap?
Does the refusal UX in CS-004 protect the free/anonymous promise without leaking moderation internals?
